nodes.summary: For every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.
nodes.title: Zenkov–Monakhov–Revin theorem (Kourovka 14.62)

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite group $G$ and every non-soluble normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ there is a maximal soluble subgroup $S$ of $H$ (a soluble subgroup $S \le H$ contained in no strictly larger soluble subgroup of $H$) such that $G = H\,N_G(S)$, where $N_G(S)$ is the normalizer of $S$ in $G$; since $H$ is normal, this says that $H$ and $N_G(S)$ generate $G$.
